The admissible record supports launch readiness at the aggregate level because the release clears readiness by 2.1 percentage points and had no severity-one rehearsal incidents. It also supports a governance posture in which residual risk can be documented and monitored through deployment. But that same admissible record does not cleanly establish that omission of a material weakness disclosure already satisfies internal policy, because the affected small-business onboarding segment misses target, is named in two paid pilot commitments, legal review remains open, and the policy requires disclosure for material limitations affecting named launch use cases unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance. The correct interpretation is not clean compliance; it is that certification can be defended as a bounded launch-readiness decision with explicit caveat that the disclosure basis is weak on the current record.
